## AI & LLM Engineering

::: {.project-card}
### [olmOCR Document Extraction Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/leonarb/olmocr-demo)

**Vision-language PDF-to-markdown pipeline, deployed as a public HuggingFace Space**

[olmOCR](https://huggingface.co/allenai/olmOCR-7B-0225-preview) is Allen Institute for AI's 7B vision-language model fine-tuned for high-fidelity document extraction — preserving tables, equations, and multi-column layouts that trip up conventional OCR pipelines. The model takes a rendered PDF page image and outputs structured markdown, handling scanned documents, academic papers, and government forms without a preprocessing pipeline.

This Space wraps the model in a Gradio interface so non-technical users can upload a PDF and get back clean markdown in one click. Under the hood: the PDF is rendered page-by-page via `pdf2image`, each page is passed to the olmOCR inference endpoint as a base64-encoded image, and the outputs are concatenated into a single downloadable `.md` file. The Space runs on a ZeroGPU allocation (A100, shared) so cold-start latency is the main UX constraint — typical throughput is ~4 seconds per page once warm.

**Stack:** Python · Gradio · HuggingFace Spaces · ZeroGPU · pdf2image · Pillow

[LLM Deployment]{.tag} [Document AI]{.tag} [Vision-Language]{.tag} [Python]{.tag} [HuggingFace]{.tag}

## Interactive Tools

::: {.project-card}
### [OKI Region Clustering Analysis Dashboard](https://benedictleonardi.shinyapps.io/clustering_analysis_dashboard/)

**Interactive TAZ-level cluster explorer with AI-generated cluster descriptions**

This Shiny dashboard lets users explore unsupervised clustering of the OKI region's Traffic Analysis Zones (TAZs) across three axes — population density, population growth, or both — with configurable cluster counts (7–12) and a year slider spanning 1990–2020. For each combination, a `mapview` choropleth maps the spatial distribution of clusters alongside histogram and trajectory plots by cluster.

The dashboard integrates an optional LLM-powered summary layer via `ellmer`: when enabled, cluster centroids are passed to a Claude prompt that returns a short verbal description of each cluster's character (e.g., "Urban, high density, centered on CBDs"), rendered inline in the UI. The AI descriptions are generated on demand and cached per configuration.

**Stack:** R · Shiny · sf · mapview · ggplot2 · ellmer (Claude API)

::: {.tags}
[Clustering]{.tag} [Geospatial]{.tag} [LLM Integration]{.tag} [R · Shiny]{.tag} [OKI Region]{.tag}
:::
:::

::: {.project-card}
### [Dynamic TAZ/County Population Projections](https://oki-data.shinyapps.io/dynamic_projections/)

**Multi-method population forecasting dashboard for the OKI region**

A Shiny-powered Quarto document that produces and compares tract- and TAZ-level population projections for the OKI metro region through 2040. Three methods are implemented side-by-side: **dynamic linear models** (DLM, treating each zone's trajectory as a state-space time series), **XGBoost** (trained on lagged demographic, land-use, and accessibility features), and **Hamilton-Perry** (a cohort-component extrapolation common in regional planning practice). Interactive Leaflet and Plotly panels let users toggle method, geography level, and forecast horizon.

**Stack:** R · Shiny · Quarto · leaflet · plotly · ggiraph · sf

::: {.tags}
[Demography]{.tag} [Forecasting]{.tag} [Time Series]{.tag} [Machine Learning]{.tag} [R · Shiny]{.tag}

## Sports & Quantitative Side Projects

::: {.project-card}
### [Braess's Paradox in Sport](https://bleonardi.github.io/Braess_Paradox_Sports/) · [GitHub](https://github.com/bleonardi/Braess_Paradox_Sports)
Does a numerical disadvantage in hockey or soccer ever produce *more* efficient scoring output? Nine NHL seasons (932K shots) reject the hypothesis with high confidence — man-up teams convert ~13% better per shot-quality unit. Soccer remains underpowered across four competition strata.

::: {.tags}
[Sports Analytics]{.tag} [Network Theory]{.tag} [Causal Inference]{.tag} [R]{.tag}
